entries.name: int-tobyte-id1-errored#0
entries.script: { (1: Int).toByte }  // JVM: PARSES at tree version 3 and throws at eval: `toByte` is in the 38-method parse-then-fail set — neither a FixedCost nor carrying a `toByte_eval` handler, so MethodCall.eval's non-FixedCost branch raises RuntimeException("Cannot find eval method"). sigma-rust refuses method id 1 at PARSE instead, which the wire arm pins.

entries.name: int-tobigint-id5-errored#1
entries.script: { (1: Int).toBigInt }  // JVM: PARSES at tree version 3 and throws at eval: `toBigInt` is in the 38-method parse-then-fail set — neither a FixedCost nor carrying a `toBigInt_eval` handler, so MethodCall.eval's non-FixedCost branch raises RuntimeException("Cannot find eval method"). sigma-rust refuses method id 5 at PARSE instead, which the wire arm pins. This is the id sigma-rust leaves out of its numeric table ALTOGETHER, so it refuses this at parse at every version while the JVM parses it at v3 — a parse-side divergence, the opposite direction to the spend one the probe expected.

entries.name: sglobal-id1-on-int-errored#2
entries.script: { SGlobal method 1 (groupGenerator) invoked on an Int receiver, db 6a 01 }  // JVM: PARSES — 0x6a is SGlobal, which has method 1 at every tree version, so rule 1016 passes — and then throws IllegalArgumentException "object is not an instance of declaring class" in reflection, the receiver being an Integer and not a SigmaDslBuilder. A DIFFERENT failure class from #0 and #1, and the tree the JVM's own below-v3 serializer emits for a numeric method call.
